messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on last week's RFC — we've had two prod incidents where multiple upstream proxies add overlapping claim sets and our RBAC mapping ends up granting both project:read and org:admin. Can we align on precedence rules?
jonathan: Yeah saw the alert. Repro steps: client -> apigw (adds agent_claims) -> ingress proxy (adds tenant_claims) -> service. The mapping code currently unions all role claims.
li: Unioning sounds dangerous. We should prefer the most-restrictive or most-specific source.
alex: Two options: 1) canonicalize at the edge (single source of truth) or 2) deterministic precedence order in mapping service.
maria: Canonicalizing at the edge is clean but needs changes across multiple proxies (burdens ops). Precedence is smaller scope but harder to reason about security-wise.
jonathan: Proposed precedence: service-issued (short-lived) > operator-issued > proxy-inserted > client-provided. That way operator overrides proxies but service ephemeral tokens are highest.
li: Matches least privilege thinking except "operator > proxy" might surprise infra teams.
alex: If we go precedence, add telemetry for every mapping decision (source weights, chosen roles) and an audit tag for fallback. Need to avoid perf blow-up.
patrick: We can emit lightweight counters per route + histogram of mapping time. Also a sampling tracer for decisions.
maria: Example claim shapes we've seen:
{
  \"sub\": \"svc-123\",
  \"claims\": [
    {\"role\": \"project:read\", \"source\": \"apigw\"},
    {\"role\": \"org:admin\", \"source\": \"ingress-proxy\"}
  ]
}
jonathan: Proposed pseudo-code for deterministic merge:
sources_order = [\"service\",\"operator\",\"ingress-proxy\",\"apigw\",\"client\"]
result = {}
for src in sources_order:
  for c in claims_from(src):
    if c.role not in result:
      result[c.role] = {\"source\": src}
# final role set = keys(result)
li: That keeps first-seen (highest priority) and prevents duplicates. What about conflicting role attributes (e.g., role with project=123 vs project=*)?
alex: Extend key to include scoping tuple: role_id + scope_identifier (project/org). When first-seen, lock it. If later claim is more-specific (project id vs wildcard), we could allow override — but that breaks simple deterministic code.
maria: Tradeoff: simplicity vs correctness. Option A: keep first-seen based on trusted source order. Option B: allow specific-to-general override if incoming has a non-wildcard project.
patrick: Prefer Option B but only if we restrict to operator/service sources. If proxy/client sends a specific project, we shouldn't elevate it above operator claims.
jonathan: So rule: service/operator can override by specificity; proxies/clients cannot. More complex but reasonable.
li: Need clear docs and tests. Also change message formats to include claim provenance and a confidence score (0-1) to support future ML heuristics.
alex: Confidence optional. For now, add boolean \"trusted_source\" for operator/service.
maria: Migration plan:
- Phase 0: shadow mode in mapping service (log decisions but don't enforce) for 2 weeks
- Phase 1: enable precedence logic behind feature flag in canary (10% traffic) for 1 week
- Phase 2: full rollout if no regressions + add audit log retention for 30d
jonathan: Who owns edge canonicalization long-term? cc @infra
li: Infra volunteers: tbd. Require proxies to stop adding redundant \"role\" claims and instead add a provenance envelope.
alex: Tests to add: unit tests for precedence matrix, integration tests with dual-proxy setups, regression test for incident payloads.
maria: Security checklist: ensure operator tokens rotated frequently; mapping code memory-safe (defend against huge claim arrays); rate-limit claim processing per request.
patrick: Ops: add metrics: mapping_decisions_total by route, mapping_conflict_samples (sampled json), mapping_latency_ms.
jonathan: Implementation note: keep mapping code pure and fast. Avoid calling external services during mapping.
li: Anyone opposed to the service/operator override policy? (vote with 👍)
alex: 👍
jonathan: 👍
patrick: 👍
maria: I'll draft a short RFC update and a migration checklist. Thanks all.
sec-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/issues/492 with title \"deterministic-claims-merge-and-precedence\" and attached logs from incidents.
maria: Added follow-up: please drop sample payloads to the issue and tag with \"incident-381\" if you have repros.
jonathan: Will add repros today.
li: I'll add unit test stubs in the mapping repo and link PR when ready.
alex: I'll coordinate with infra about edge canonicalization long-term.
patrick: Will add metrics dashboard draft (grafana) — will post link in the issue later.
